sections.html:
Kenner is the largest incorporated suburb of New Orleans, in Jefferson Parish on the west side of the metro area. It had 66,448 residents in the 2020 census, the sixth most populous city in Louisiana. It covers about 15 square miles, with Lake Pontchartrain on the north edge and the Mississippi River on the south. Metairie and River Ridge lie to the east and St. Charles Parish to the west, so a Kenner house is rarely far from a levee, a drainage canal or a pumping station.

Most of the housing north of Airline Highway did not exist before the late 1950s. Swamp was drained and filled, and Interstate 10 plus road improvements in the 1960s pushed the suburb outward fast. Population climbed from 5,535 in 1950 to 66,382 by 1980. Many Kenner houses are mid-century builds on filled ground, so buyers in the northern subdivisions often ask about drainage and settling. The older part of town sits nearer the river, around Rivertown, which was founded in 1855 by Minor Kenner. Interstate 10, U.S. 61 (Airline Drive) and Louisiana 49 (Williams Boulevard) are the main roads.

Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport sits inside the Kenner city limits, just south of Interstate 10. It brings aircraft noise to some blocks and a steady stream of travelers and airport workers who need housing nearby.

You do not need to hide noise. The Louisiana disclosure form asks what you know about the property, and an honest answer about overhead aircraft protects you.

  • Ask a neighbor or two how often planes pass over at different times of day.
  • Keep any insulation or window upgrades you did and mention them.
  • For a buyer who travels for work, a short drive to the terminal is a real selling point.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a Kenner house?
sections.html:
A Kenner owner pays parish taxes through the Jefferson Parish Sheriff, who is the tax collector, and also receives a separate bill from the City of Kenner. The Jefferson Parish Assessor sets value but does not set the rate. Call the assessor at 504-362-4100 with questions about your assessment.

Tax ruleJefferson Parish detail
Residential assessment ratio10% of fair market value
Homestead exemptionFirst $7,500 of assessed value, equal to $75,000 of market value, on an owner-occupied home
Kenner 2025 combined millage0.10625 (parish 0.07809, city 0.02816)
ReappraisalAt least every four years; the last full one was 2016

Kenner is ward 92. The combined millage works out to about 106 mills. The homestead exemption is not subtracted when the city part is figured, so the city rate applies to the full assessed value.

The exemption ends when you sell or move out, and only one homestead exemption is allowed on a home in Louisiana. A buyer who wants it has to appear in person at the assessor's office with a recorded copy of the act of sale and a photo ID showing the property address. That is why the recorded act matters to the next owner. A frozen assessed value for seniors or some disabled owners is tied to the owner and the home, and it does not pass to a buyer as a promise.

sections.h2: Tax calendar and selling in the fall
sections.html: Assessors file the parish roll by November 15, and taxes are due by December 31. Unpaid taxes become delinquent the next day and accrue interest at one percent per month under R.S. 47:2127. If you sell in the fall, ask the closing notary how the current year's bill will be handled so nothing is left owing on a house you no longer own.

sections.h2: How is a house sale made legal in Louisiana?
sections.html:
A transfer of land or a house must be made by authentic act or by an act under private signature. Under Article 1839 of the Civil Code, the paper affects outside parties only once it is filed for registry in the parish where the property sits. For Kenner that parish is Jefferson, so the act of sale must be signed and then recorded with the parish clerk before the transfer protects the buyer against third parties.

  • The act of sale is signed at closing, usually with a notary present.
  • It is then filed for registry with the Jefferson Parish clerk.
  • The buyer later brings a recorded copy to the assessor for homestead.
  • Any mortgage you still owe is paid from proceeds and cancelled of record.

Under R.S. 9:3198, a seller of residential property completes a property disclosure form and gives it to the buyer no later than the time the buyer makes an offer. If the form arrives after the offer, the buyer can cancel the contract or withdraw the offer within 72 hours of receiving it, not counting weekends and holidays, and deposits come back. The form is not a warranty, and a seller who passes along a public body's or a professional's report in good faith is not liable for its mistakes. If you do not know something, the form lets you say so.

Buyers in Kenner care most about water, wind and noise. Note any past flood claims, roof replacements and drainage work. Hurricane Katrina in 2005 brought widespread East Bank flooding in Jefferson Parish, especially in Metairie and Kenner, so buyers will ask.

sections.h2: What city rules apply if a Kenner house is empty or in poor shape?
sections.html:
The City of Kenner runs an abandoned property registration program under Ordinance 10455, and its Inspection and Code Enforcement Department handles building permits and complaints. An annual registration form is required for each vacant property. If you inherited a house and left it empty, find out whether it is registered, because an empty house that draws complaints can build up fines.

The code department is at 1926 18th Street, Kenner, LA 70062, and the permits desk is at 504-468-4062. Ask about any unfinished permit so you can tell a buyer what is still open.

Selling as-is can end that exposure. A cash buyer takes on the registration, the repairs and the permit work, and you do not need to finish open projects first.

sections.h2: Steps from offer to closing in Kenner
sections.html: After you accept an offer, the notary opens a title search and your lender supplies a payoff. Gather your deed, tax bill, flood and roof records and any permit paperwork. A financed buyer adds an appraisal and inspection, while a cash buyer can close once the title work is clear. At the signing, your loan balance, unpaid taxes and recording fees come out of the proceeds. Ask for the settlement statement early so you can question any charge before you sign.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on a house in Kenner?
faqs.a: The Jefferson Parish Sheriff collects parish property tax, and the City of Kenner sends its own bill. The Jefferson Parish Assessor sets the value but does not set the rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kenner house that has an open code complaint?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell it in its current condition, though you should tell the buyer about the complaint. Call the Kenner Inspection and Code Enforcement Department to find out what is open and whether the property is on the abandoned property registry.

faqs.q: Does the buyer keep my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The exemption is canceled when you sell or move. The buyer applies in person at the Jefferson Parish Assessor with a recorded act of sale and photo ID.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a disclosure form in Louisiana?
faqs.a: Yes. The seller must deliver the property disclosure form no later than the time the buyer makes an offer. A late form gives the buyer 72 hours to back out.

faqs.q: Does airport noise change what I have to say?
faqs.a: The form asks what you know about the property, so mention noise if it affects the house. Describing it plainly is safer than leaving it out.
